about: Differences between the local QA lab and production that are expected. qa-lab/parity.mjs reports these as explained; any other difference fails the check. Each reason is repeated in qa-lab/README.md.

differences.reason: Cron jobs are created INACTIVE on purpose; production's definitions (name, schedule, command, user) match exactly. Enable one locally with cron.alter_job(<id>, active := true).
The local image ships only pg_net 0.20.3 (production 0.19.5); its objects live in schema net either way, and its extension row is recorded under schema extensions locally, public in production.
Production-only login role the Supabase CLI uses; it holds no application privileges.
Local Realtime container's own bookkeeping schema.
Local stack's database-webhook schema; production has no database webhooks.
QA-lab marker schema (qa_lab.applied records when and from which catalog the schema was built).
Default privileges of the local-only supabase_functions schema.
Default privileges of the local-only supabase_functions schema.
Default privileges of the local-only supabase_functions schema.
app_secrets holds production AI provider keys; the lab never copies them, and leaves the table empty.

Supabase platform object that production's (newer) auth or storage-api version has and the local image (CLI 2.109.1: storage-api v1.62.5, gotrue v2.192.0) does not: auth MFA recovery codes and SCIM tables, new storage.search*/list* signatures, and the storage bucket-control guards (storage.protect_bucket_control_columns, storage.enforce_bucket_lifecycle_service_role) behind production's protect_bucket_control_* triggers on storage.buckets.
Supabase platform object that only the local image has: older storage.search*/list* signatures, storage.iceberg_* tables, and Realtime's daily realtime.messages_* partitions.
The local pg_cron setup leaves postgres with TRIGGER on cron.job_run_details; production does not. No application object creates a trigger there.
Realtime's own migration bookkeeping table: the local Realtime container grants it differently. The application never reads it.
